query: Why did hardware incidents spike in the anomaly window?

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: Identifies hardware vs other categories; needed to define/filter the outcome group. It is more a stratifier of the outcome (hardware is named in query) than a surfaced common cause; largely descriptive of the outcome itself.

per_column.name: failure_mode
per_column.rationale: Describes the mechanism of failure (overheating, not_powering_on, physical_damage). Could serve as a candidate cause of hardware incidents; surfaced from text and plausibly explanatory of the spike.

per_column.name: incident_action_type
per_column.rationale: break_fix/installation etc. is a downstream response to the incident, on the path after the incident occurs, not a common cause of both a cause and the outcome.

per_column.name: affected_asset_scope
per_column.rationale: server_infrastructure vs end_user_device etc. plausibly affects both the failure mode (treatment) and the propensity to generate hardware incidents; surfaced from data, a candidate common cause.

per_column.name: software_update_trigger
per_column.rationale: A boolean candidate cause: whether a software update/patch triggered the incident. Timing of updates could drive the spike; a genuine attributable treatment surfaced from data.

per_column.name: recurrence_signal
per_column.rationale: Whether the incident recurs is a consequence of the incident, not a prior common cause; conditioning on it risks selection bias rather than confounding control.

per_column.name: is_repeat_caller
per_column.rationale: Repeat callers may both experience more failures and be more likely to log incidents, plausibly a common cause of reporting propensity and observed incident counts; surfaced from data.

judge.rationale: The set supplies plausible treatments (software_update_trigger as a candidate cause, failure_mode as mechanism), satisfying part (a). For part (b), a couple of surfaced variables (affected_asset_scope, is_repeat_caller) could act as common causes and were not named in the query, showing some genuine confounder discovery. However several columns are mediators (incident_action_type) or colliders (recurrence_signal) mislabelled as explanatory, incident_category largely restates the outcome definition, and no confounder is a clearly strong common cause of both a specific treatment and the outcome. The causal estimation is only weakly set up, so confounder quality is moderate-to-low.
